note: Physics round 3: four data passages (velocity-time table, cell readings, heating curve, pendulum data) and applied/calculation items across the JAMB syllabus.

passages.title: Velocity-time readings for a car
passages.text:
The velocity of a car travelling along a
straight road was recorded every two
seconds. The readings are shown below.

Time (s)         0   2   4   6   8  10  12
Velocity (m/s)   0   6  12  12  12   6   0

passages.title: Terminal p.d. of a cell at different currents
passages.text:
A cell was connected to a variable
resistor, an ammeter and a voltmeter. The
terminal p.d. V was read for several
values of the current I.

Current I (A)    0.5   1.0   1.5   2.0
Terminal V (V)   2.7   2.4   2.1   1.8

passages.title: Heating curve of a solid
passages.text:
0.1 kg of a solid substance was heated in
an insulated container by a 50 W heater
and its temperature was recorded every two
minutes.

Time (min)      0   2   4   6   8  10  12
Temp (°C)      20  40  60  60  60  80 100

passages.title: Simple pendulum experiment
passages.text:
A student measured the period T of a
simple pendulum for several lengths l by
timing 20 complete oscillations with a
stopwatch. The results are shown below.

Length l (m)    0.25   0.49   0.81   1.00
Period T (s)     1.0    1.4    1.8    2.0

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: From the readings above, the acceleration of the car during the first 4 seconds is
questions.explanation: Acceleration = change in velocity ÷ time = (12 − 0)/4 = 3.0 m/s².

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: From the readings above, the distance covered by the car during the first 4 seconds is
questions.explanation: Distance = area under the velocity-time graph = ½ × 4 s × 12 m/s = 24 m.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: From the readings above, between the 4th and the 8th second the car was
questions.explanation: The velocity stays at 12 m/s throughout that interval, so the acceleration is zero and the car moves with constant velocity.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: From the readings above, the total distance travelled by the car in the 12 seconds is
questions.explanation: Areas under the graph: ½ × 4 × 12 = 24 m, then 12 × 4 = 48 m, then ½ × 4 × 12 = 24 m; total 96 m.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: From the readings above, the average speed of the car for the whole journey is
questions.explanation: Average speed = total distance ÷ total time = 96 m ÷ 12 s = 8 m/s.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: From the readings above, the retardation of the car during the last 4 seconds is
questions.explanation: Velocity falls from 12 m/s to 0 in 4 s: retardation = 12/4 = 3.0 m/s².

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: From the readings above, the e.m.f. of the cell is
questions.explanation: V = E − Ir. Between I = 0.5 A and 1.0 A the p.d. falls 0.3 V, so r = 0.6 Ω and E = 2.7 + 0.5 × 0.6 = 3.0 V (the intercept of the V–I graph).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: From the readings above, the internal resistance of the cell is
questions.explanation: Each extra 0.5 A of current lowers the terminal p.d. by 0.3 V: r = 0.3/0.5 = 0.6 Ω, the magnitude of the slope of the V–I graph.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: From the readings above, the resistance of the external circuit when the current was 2.0 A is

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: From the readings above, the 'lost volts' inside the cell when the current was 1.5 A is
questions.explanation: Lost volts = E − V = 3.0 − 2.1 = 0.9 V (equal to Ir = 1.5 × 0.6).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: From the readings above, the power delivered to the external circuit when the current was 1.0 A is

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In the experiment above, the terminal p.d. fell as the current increased because
questions.A: the voltmeter drew a larger share of the current at higher readings
questions.B: the external resistor became hot and its resistance increased
questions.C: the chemical e.m.f. of the cell fell steadily as the current rose
questions.D: more of the e.m.f. was dropped across the cell's own internal resistance
questions.explanation: The p.d. across the internal resistance, Ir, grows with current, leaving less of the e.m.f. across the terminals.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: From the readings above, the melting point of the substance is
questions.explanation: The temperature stayed constant at 60 °C while the solid was changing into liquid.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: From the readings above, the time taken for the substance to melt completely was
questions.explanation: The temperature remained at 60 °C from the 4th to the 8th minute, i.e. for 4 minutes.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: From the readings above, the specific heat capacity of the solid is
questions.explanation: In the first 4 minutes the heater supplied 50 × 240 = 12,000 J and the temperature rose 40 K: c = 12,000/(0.1 × 40) = 3,000 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: From the readings above, the specific latent heat of fusion of the substance is
questions.explanation: Melting took 4 minutes, during which 50 × 240 = 12,000 J was supplied to 0.1 kg: L = 12,000/0.1 = 1.2 × 10⁵ J/kg.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In the experiment above, the temperature did not rise between the 4th and 8th minute because the heat supplied was
questions.C: increasing the kinetic energy of the molecules
questions.D: being used to break the bonds holding the solid together
questions.explanation: During a change of state the energy supplied increases the potential energy of the molecules (separating them) rather than their kinetic energy, so the temperature is constant.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: From the readings above, the specific heat capacity of the liquid compared with that of the solid is
questions.explanation: The liquid also rose 40 K (60 °C to 100 °C) in 4 minutes with the same heater, so the same energy produced the same temperature rise in the same mass.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: From the data above, a graph of T² against l would be
questions.A: a curve passing through the origin
questions.C: a straight line with a positive intercept
questions.D: a straight line through the origin
questions.explanation: T = 2π√(l/g) gives T² = (4π²/g) l, so T² is directly proportional to l: the points (0.25, 1.0), (0.49, 1.96), (0.81, 3.24) and (1.00, 4.0) lie on a line through the origin.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Using the data above for l = 1.00 m, the value of the acceleration due to gravity is approximately (π² ≈ 9.87)

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The data above show that when the length of the pendulum is made four times as great, the period
questions.explanation: From 0.25 m to 1.00 m the period rises from 1.0 s to 2.0 s: T is proportional to √l, so four times the length doubles the period.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In the experiment above, the student timed 20 oscillations instead of one in order to
questions.A: make the pendulum swing faster and so save time in the laboratory
questions.B: stop the string from stretching while the readings are being taken
questions.C: increase the amplitude of the swing so that it is easier to count
questions.D: reduce the effect of reaction-time error on the measured period
questions.explanation: The stopwatch error (about 0.2 s) is spread over 20 swings, so the error in one period becomes twenty times smaller.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: From the data above, the number of complete oscillations the 0.25 m pendulum makes in one minute is
questions.explanation: Period = 1.0 s, so in 60 s it completes 60/1.0 = 60 oscillations.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: If the pendulum in the experiment above were taken to the Moon, where g is about one-sixth of its value on Earth, the period of the 1.00 m pendulum would be
questions.explanation: T = 2π√(l/g): a smaller g gives a longer period (about 2.0 × √6 ≈ 4.9 s).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The dimensions of pressure are
questions.explanation: Pressure = force/area = MLT⁻² ÷ L² = ML⁻¹T⁻².

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A micrometer screw gauge with no zero error has a sleeve reading of 5.5 mm and the 23rd division of the thimble on the reference line. If the thimble has 50 divisions and the pitch is 0.5 mm, the reading is
questions.explanation: Each thimble division is 0.5/50 = 0.01 mm; reading = 5.5 + 23 × 0.01 = 5.73 mm.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The main scale of a vernier caliper reads 2.3 cm and the 6th vernier division coincides with a main-scale mark. If the vernier has 10 divisions equal to 9 mm, the length measured is
questions.explanation: The least count is 0.1 mm = 0.01 cm; length = 2.3 + 6 × 0.01 = 2.36 cm.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A student lists mass, weight, time and temperature. The quantity in the list that is NOT a fundamental quantity is
questions.explanation: Weight is a force (mass × acceleration due to gravity) and is derived from mass, length and time.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A rectangular block measures 2.0 cm by 3.0 cm by 4.0 cm and has a mass of 60 g. Its density is
questions.explanation: Volume = 2 × 3 × 4 = 24 cm³; density = 60/24 = 2.5 g/cm³.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The number of significant figures in the measurement 0.00450 m is
questions.explanation: Leading zeros are not significant but the trailing zero after the 5 is: 4, 5 and 0 give three significant figures.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The most suitable instrument for measuring the diameter of a thin copper wire is a
questions.explanation: A micrometer screw gauge reads to 0.01 mm, the precision needed for a wire a fraction of a millimetre thick.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A student measuring the period of a pendulum repeats the timing five times and takes the average. This procedure reduces
questions.explanation: Random errors vary unpredictably from reading to reading, so averaging several readings reduces their effect; systematic errors are not removed by averaging.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A micrometer screw gauge has a zero error of +0.02 mm. When used to measure a ball bearing it reads 3.45 mm. The true diameter is
questions.explanation: A positive zero error is subtracted from the observed reading: 3.45 − 0.02 = 3.43 mm.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The force on a body moving through a fluid is given by F = kv², where v is the velocity. The dimensions of the constant k are
questions.explanation: k = F/v² = MLT⁻² ÷ (L²T⁻²) = ML⁻¹.

questions.q: A car travelling at 72 km/h has a speed in metres per second of

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Which of the following pairs of physical quantities have the same unit?
questions.explanation: Impulse (N s) equals change of momentum (kg m s⁻¹); the two units are identical.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A stopwatch reading is taken with the eye not directly above the pointer. The error introduced is described as
questions.A: a random error due to reaction time
questions.explanation: Reading a scale from an angle displaces the apparent position of the pointer; this is parallax and is avoided by viewing at right angles to the scale.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The volume of a stone that is too large for a measuring cylinder is best found by
questions.A: measuring its length, breadth and height with a metre rule
questions.B: weighing it on a beam balance and dividing by the density of water
questions.C: lowering it into a full displacement can and measuring the overflow
questions.D: wrapping a tape measure round it and cubing the circumference
questions.explanation: The volume of water displaced equals the volume of the irregular stone.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A student describes a car as moving at 60 km/h due north. Because a direction is given, the quantity she has stated is the car's
questions.explanation: Speed together with a stated direction is velocity, a vector quantity; speed on its own is a scalar.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A force of 20 N acts at 60° to the horizontal. Its horizontal component is
questions.explanation: Horizontal component = F cos θ = 20 × cos 60° = 20 × 0.5 = 10 N.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A boat is pulled by two ropes at right angles to each other with forces of 5 N and 12 N. The magnitude of the resultant pull on the boat is

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two forces of 10 N each act at a point with an angle of 120° between them. The magnitude of their resultant is

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A boat that can travel at 4 m/s in still water heads straight across a river flowing at 3 m/s. The resultant velocity of the boat is
questions.explanation: The two velocities are perpendicular: resultant = √(4² + 3²) = 5 m/s.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two forces of 7 N and 3 N act on a body. The maximum and minimum possible magnitudes of their resultant are respectively
questions.explanation: The resultant is greatest (7 + 3 = 10 N) when the forces are in the same direction and least (7 − 3 = 4 N) when they are opposite.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A cyclist rides 12 km due west and then 5 km due south. The magnitude of her displacement from the starting point is
questions.explanation: Displacement = √(12² + 5²) = √169 = 13 km, although the distance travelled is 17 km.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two forces of 8 N and 6 N act at right angles on a body. The force that must be applied to keep the body in equilibrium is
questions.A: 10 N opposite to the resultant of the two forces
questions.C: 2 N opposite to the 6 N force
questions.D: 10 N along the resultant of the two forces
questions.explanation: The resultant is √(8² + 6²) = 10 N; a third force equal and opposite to it (the equilibrant) gives zero net force.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A projectile is fired at 50 m/s at an angle of 30° above the horizontal. The vertical component of its initial velocity is
questions.explanation: Vertical component = u sin θ = 50 × sin 30° = 25 m/s.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Which of the following pairs consists of scalar quantities only?
questions.explanation: Work and energy have magnitude but no direction; each of the other pairs contains vectors.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two forces of 6 N and 8 N act at a point with an angle of 60° between them. The magnitude of their resultant is approximately

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Car A travels east at 80 km/h while car B travels west at 60 km/h on the same road. The velocity of A relative to B is
questions.explanation: Relative velocity = v_A − v_B = 80 − (−60) = 140 km/h towards the east.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A car moves round a circular track at a constant speed of 20 m/s. Which statement is correct?
questions.A: its velocity changes because its direction changes
questions.B: its velocity is constant because its speed is constant
questions.C: its acceleration is zero because its speed is constant
questions.D: no resultant force acts on it while it is on the track
questions.explanation: Velocity is a vector; a continuous change of direction means the velocity changes, so the car accelerates (towards the centre) and a centripetal force acts on it.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A body is acted upon by a 3 N force pointing north and a 4 N force pointing east. The direction of the resultant makes an angle with the east direction of approximately
questions.explanation: tan θ = 3/4 = 0.75, so θ = 37° north of east.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A car starts from rest and accelerates uniformly at 2 m/s² for 10 s. The distance it covers is
questions.explanation: s = ut + ½at² = 0 + ½ × 2 × 10² = 100 m.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A stone dropped into a well hits the water 2 s later. Taking g = 10 m/s², the depth of the water surface below the top of the well is
questions.explanation: s = ½gt² = ½ × 10 × 2² = 20 m.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A ball is kicked with a velocity of 20 m/s at 30° to the horizontal. Taking g = 10 m/s², its time of flight is

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A ball is kicked with a velocity of 20 m/s at 30° to the horizontal. Taking g = 10 m/s², its horizontal range is approximately

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A projectile is launched at 20 m/s at 30° to the horizontal. Taking g = 10 m/s², the maximum height it reaches is

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A stone tied to a string is whirled in a horizontal circle at 2 revolutions per second. Its angular velocity is

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A 1,000 kg car goes round a bend of radius 50 m at 10 m/s. The centripetal force required is
questions.explanation: F = mv²/r = 1,000 × 10²/50 = 2,000 N, supplied by friction between the tyres and the road.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A simple pendulum swings between two extreme positions. Its speed is greatest
questions.B: midway between the lowest point and an extreme
questions.C: at the lowest point of the swing
questions.explanation: In simple harmonic motion the speed is maximum at the equilibrium (centre) position where the displacement is zero.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: For a body performing simple harmonic motion, the acceleration is greatest when the body is
questions.A: at the centre of the motion
questions.explanation: Acceleration is proportional to displacement (a = −ω²x), so it is largest at maximum displacement, where the body momentarily stops.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The velocity-time graph of a car is a straight line sloping downwards towards the time axis. The car is
questions.explanation: The slope of a velocity-time graph is the acceleration; a constant negative slope means uniform retardation.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A train 100 m long passes a signal post in 5 s at constant speed. The time it takes to pass completely through a station platform 300 m long is
questions.explanation: Speed = 100/5 = 20 m/s. To clear the platform the train must travel 100 + 300 = 400 m, taking 400/20 = 20 s.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A ball thrown vertically upwards with a speed of 30 m/s returns to the thrower's hand after (g = 10 m/s²)
questions.explanation: Time to the top = u/g = 3 s and the same time to fall back, so 6 s in all.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A ball is thrown vertically upwards at 30 m/s. Taking g = 10 m/s², its speed when it is 25 m above the point of projection is

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A cyclist moving at 12 m/s applies the brakes and comes to rest in 4 s with uniform retardation. The distance travelled while braking is
questions.explanation: Distance = average velocity × time = ½ × 12 × 4 = 24 m.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Passengers standing in a bus lurch forward when the bus stops suddenly. This is explained by
questions.C: the centripetal force on the bus
questions.explanation: By Newton's first law a body keeps moving unless a force acts on it; the passengers' bodies continue forward while the bus stops.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A raindrop falls through the air at constant velocity. This happens because
questions.A: the air resistance on the drop equals its weight
questions.B: gravity stops acting on the drop
questions.D: the upthrust of the air equals the weight
questions.explanation: At terminal velocity the resistive force balances the weight, so the net force and the acceleration are zero.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two identical balls are released from the same height at the same instant; one is dropped and the other is thrown horizontally. Ignoring air resistance,
questions.C: both balls land at the same time
questions.explanation: The vertical motion of both balls is the same free fall from rest; the horizontal velocity of the thrown ball does not affect how long it takes to fall.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A uniform plank 4 m long weighing 200 N rests on a pivot 1 m from one end. The vertical force needed at that end to keep the plank horizontal is
questions.explanation: The weight acts at the centre, 1 m beyond the pivot; taking moments: F × 1 = 200 × 1, so F = 200 N.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A uniform metre rule is supported at its centre. A 50 g mass is hung from the 20 cm mark. To restore the balance, a 100 g mass must be hung from the
questions.explanation: Clockwise moment = anticlockwise moment: 100 × d = 50 × 30, so d = 15 cm on the other side, i.e. the 65 cm mark.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A uniform metre rule balances horizontally on a knife edge at its 30 cm mark when a 100 g mass hangs from the 5 cm mark. The mass of the rule is
questions.explanation: The rule's weight acts at 50 cm, 20 cm from the pivot; 100 × 25 = W × 20 gives W = 125 g.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two equal and opposite forces of 5 N act on a steering wheel at points 0.4 m apart. The moment of the couple is
questions.explanation: Moment of a couple = one force × perpendicular distance between the forces = 5 × 0.4 = 2 N m.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A racing car is built with a low centre of gravity and a wide wheel base in order to
questions.explanation: A body is stable when its centre of gravity is low and its base wide, so that tilting does not move the weight's line of action outside the base.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: For a rigid body acted on by several coplanar forces to be in equilibrium,
questions.A: the resultant force and the resultant moment must both be zero
questions.B: only the resultant force on the body must be zero
questions.C: only the resultant moment about any point must be zero
questions.D: all the forces must be equal in magnitude and parallel
questions.explanation: Zero resultant force prevents translation and zero resultant moment about any point prevents rotation.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A swimmer pushes the water backwards with her hands and moves forwards. This illustrates
questions.explanation: The backward force on the water is matched by an equal and opposite forward force of the water on the swimmer.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A 4 kg block is pulled along a horizontal floor at constant velocity by a horizontal force of 8 N. Taking g = 10 m/s², the coefficient of kinetic friction is
questions.explanation: At constant velocity friction equals the pull: μ = F/R = 8/(4 × 10) = 0.2.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A 10 kg block slides down a smooth (frictionless) plane inclined at 30° to the horizontal. Taking g = 10 m/s², its acceleration is
questions.explanation: a = g sin θ = 10 × sin 30° = 5 m/s²; the mass cancels out.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A 2 kg mass hangs from a spring balance in a lift. Taking g = 10 m/s², the balance reads, when the lift accelerates upwards at 2 m/s²,
questions.explanation: T − mg = ma, so T = m(g + a) = 2 × 12 = 24 N.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A person standing on a weighing scale in a lift notices that the scale reads zero. The lift must be
questions.explanation: The scale reads m(g − a); it reads zero only when the downward acceleration equals g, i.e. free fall.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A 5 kg picture hangs from two strings, each making 60° with the vertical. Taking g = 10 m/s², the tension in each string is
questions.explanation: The vertical components support the weight: 2T cos 60° = 50, so T = 50 N.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The centre of gravity of a uniform triangular lamina lies at
questions.B: the midpoint of its shortest side
questions.C: the midpoint of its longest side
questions.D: the point where its medians meet
questions.explanation: The medians of a triangle meet at the centroid, one-third of the way along each median from the side; a uniform lamina balances at this point.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A 1,500 kg car accelerates uniformly from rest to 20 m/s in 10 s. The resultant force acting on it is

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A ladder leaning against a smooth wall is prevented from slipping mainly by
questions.A: friction between the ladder and the ground
questions.C: the reaction of the smooth wall
questions.explanation: The smooth wall can only push horizontally on the ladder; the ground's friction supplies the horizontal force that balances it.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A boy pulls a load 10 m along a horizontal floor with a rope inclined at 60° to the floor, using a force of 100 N. The work done is

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A 0.5 kg ball is dropped from a height of 20 m. Ignoring air resistance and taking g = 10 m/s², its speed just before it hits the ground is

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A pendulum bob is pulled aside until it is 0.2 m above its lowest position and released. Taking g = 10 m/s², its speed as it passes through the lowest point is
questions.explanation: Potential energy becomes kinetic energy: v = √(2gh) = √(2 × 10 × 0.2) = 2 m/s.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A crane lifts a 500 kg load through a height of 20 m in 25 s. Taking g = 10 m/s², the power developed is

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An electric motor rated 2 kW lifts a 100 kg load through 15 m in 10 s. Taking g = 10 m/s², the efficiency of the motor is

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Which of the following has the greatest kinetic energy?
questions.A: a 2 kg body moving at 4 m/s
questions.B: a 4 kg body moving at 2 m/s
questions.C: an 8 kg body moving at 1 m/s
questions.D: a 1 kg body moving at 5 m/s
questions.explanation: KE = ½mv²: 16 J, 8 J, 4 J and 12.5 J respectively; the 2 kg body at 4 m/s has the most.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A porter carries a 20 kg load up a flight of 12 steps, each 0.25 m high. Taking g = 10 m/s², the work done against gravity is

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A spring of force constant 200 N/m is stretched by 0.1 m. The elastic potential energy stored in it is

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: If the speed of a car is doubled, the distance it needs to stop with the same braking force is
questions.explanation: Work done by the brakes (F × d) equals the kinetic energy ½mv²; doubling v makes the energy, and hence the stopping distance, four times as great.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A car engine develops 40 kW while the car travels at a steady 20 m/s on a level road. The total resistive force on the car is
questions.explanation: Power = force × velocity, so F = 40,000/20 = 2,000 N; at steady speed the driving force equals the resistance.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In a hydroelectric power station the energy changes that take place are
questions.explanation: Water stored high in the dam has potential energy, gains kinetic energy as it falls and turns turbines that drive generators.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A stone is whirled in a horizontal circle at constant speed. The work done by the centripetal force during one revolution is
questions.B: equal to the kinetic energy of the stone
questions.C: equal to the force multiplied by the circumference
questions.D: equal to the weight multiplied by the radius
questions.explanation: The centripetal force is always perpendicular to the displacement, so it does no work and the speed stays constant.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A 10 g bullet moving at 400 m/s penetrates 20 cm into a block of wood before stopping. The average resistive force of the wood is

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A 3 kg body is thrown vertically upwards with 100 J of kinetic energy. Taking g = 10 m/s² and ignoring air resistance, the maximum height it reaches is
questions.explanation: At the top all the kinetic energy has become potential energy: h = 100/(3 × 10) = 3.3 m.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Which of the following is a renewable source of energy?
questions.explanation: Sunlight is continually replenished, whereas fossil fuels are used up faster than they form.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A 1,500 kg car travelling at 20 m/s and a 30,000 kg lorry crawling at 1 m/s have
questions.explanation: Momentum = mass × velocity: 1,500 × 20 = 30,000 kg m/s for the car and 30,000 × 1 = 30,000 kg m/s for the lorry; their kinetic energies (300 kJ and 15 kJ) differ.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A 0.2 kg ball moving at 10 m/s is caught and brought to rest in 0.05 s. The average force exerted on the ball is
questions.explanation: Force = change in momentum ÷ time = (0.2 × 10)/0.05 = 40 N.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A 40 kg boy standing on a smooth skateboard throws a 2 kg ball horizontally at 10 m/s. The boy and skateboard move backwards at
questions.explanation: Momentum is conserved: 40 × v = 2 × 10, so v = 0.5 m/s in the opposite direction.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A 4 kg trolley moving at 6 m/s catches up with a 2 kg trolley at rest on the same track and couples to it. The speed of the coupled trolleys is
questions.explanation: Total momentum before = 4 × 6 = 24 kg m/s = (4 + 2) × v, so v = 4 m/s.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In a perfectly elastic collision between two bodies,
questions.A: both momentum and kinetic energy are conserved
questions.explanation: Momentum is conserved in every collision; kinetic energy is conserved only in elastic collisions. Bodies that stick together undergo a perfectly inelastic collision.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A fielder draws his hands backwards while catching a fast cricket ball in order to
questions.A: increase the momentum of the ball
questions.B: reduce the kinetic energy of the ball to zero instantly
questions.C: increase the time of impact and so reduce the force on his hands
questions.explanation: Force = change of momentum ÷ time; spreading the same momentum change over a longer time reduces the average force.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A car jack raises a 4,000 N car when a force of 200 N is applied to its handle. The mechanical advantage of the jack is
questions.explanation: Mechanical advantage = load ÷ effort = 4,000/200 = 20.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A machine has a mechanical advantage of 4 and a velocity ratio of 5. Its efficiency is
questions.explanation: Efficiency = (MA/VR) × 100 = 4/5 × 100 = 80%.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A screw jack has a pitch of 5 mm and a handle of length 20 cm. Its velocity ratio is approximately
questions.explanation: VR = 2πR/pitch = 2π × 200 mm/5 mm ≈ 251.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A wheel and axle has a wheel of radius 30 cm and an axle of radius 5 cm. Its velocity ratio is
questions.explanation: VR = radius of wheel ÷ radius of axle = 30/5 = 6.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The velocity ratio of an inclined plane that makes an angle of 30° with the horizontal is
questions.explanation: VR = length of plane ÷ height = 1/sin 30° = 2.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A pulley system with a velocity ratio of 5 is 80% efficient. The effort needed to raise a load of 400 N with it is
questions.explanation: MA = efficiency × VR = 0.8 × 5 = 4; effort = load/MA = 400/4 = 100 N.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A wheelbarrow is an example of a lever in which
questions.A: the fulcrum is between the load and the effort
questions.B: the load and effort act at the same point
questions.C: the effort is between the fulcrum and the load
questions.D: the load is between the fulcrum and the effort
questions.explanation: In a wheelbarrow the wheel is the fulcrum, the load sits in the tray and the effort is applied at the handles: a second-class lever.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The efficiency of a practical machine is always less than 100% mainly because
questions.A: some of the work input is wasted against friction and in lifting moving parts
questions.B: the load is always heavier than the effort applied to the machine
questions.C: the velocity ratio of the machine is always less than one
questions.D: energy is destroyed inside the machine whenever it is used
questions.explanation: Some of the work input is wasted as heat due to friction and in lifting the movable parts of the machine itself.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A gear wheel with 20 teeth drives another gear wheel with 60 teeth. The velocity ratio of the arrangement is
questions.explanation: VR = number of teeth on driven wheel ÷ number on driving wheel = 60/20 = 3.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A spring is 20 cm long when unloaded and 24 cm long when a 2 N weight hangs from it. Within the elastic limit, its length when a 5 N weight hangs from it is
questions.explanation: 2 N gives 4 cm extension, so 5 N gives 10 cm; length = 20 + 10 = 30 cm.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A wire 2 m long with cross-sectional area 1.0 × 10⁻⁶ m² stretches by 1.0 mm under a load of 100 N. The Young's modulus of the material is
questions.explanation: Stress = 100/10⁻⁶ = 10⁸ N/m²; strain = 10⁻³/2 = 5 × 10⁻⁴; E = stress/strain = 2.0 × 10¹¹ N/m².

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The wall of a dam is built much thicker at the bottom than at the top because
questions.A: the water is colder at the bottom
questions.B: the bottom carries the weight of the top
questions.C: the pressure of the water increases with depth
questions.D: the water flows faster at the bottom
questions.explanation: Pressure in a liquid = hρg, so it is greatest at the base of the dam and the wall must be strongest there.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A solid of volume 200 cm³ is completely immersed in water of density 1,000 kg/m³. Taking g = 10 m/s², the upthrust on it is
questions.explanation: Upthrust = weight of water displaced = 200 × 10⁻⁶ m³ × 1,000 × 10 = 2 N.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A block of wood of density 0.6 g/cm³ floats in water. The fraction of its volume below the water surface is
questions.explanation: For a floating body, the fraction submerged = density of body ÷ density of liquid = 0.6/1.0 = 0.6.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A density bottle weighs 20 g empty, 70 g full of water and 60 g full of a liquid. The relative density of the liquid is
questions.explanation: RD = mass of liquid ÷ mass of equal volume of water = (60 − 20)/(70 − 20) = 0.8.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A steel needle placed carefully on the surface of water floats although steel is denser than water. This is due to
questions.explanation: The water surface behaves like a stretched elastic skin that supports the light needle.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: When a narrow glass tube is dipped into water the water rises in the tube, but when it is dipped into mercury the mercury level in the tube is depressed. This is because
questions.A: water wets glass (adhesion > cohesion) while mercury does not
questions.B: water is much less dense than mercury and so rises more easily
questions.C: mercury is a metal and metals are always repelled by glass
questions.D: the tube is too narrow for the heavy mercury to enter it
questions.explanation: Capillary rise occurs when the liquid's adhesion to the glass exceeds its own cohesion; for mercury cohesion is stronger, giving a convex meniscus and depression.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A steel ball falling through glycerine soon reaches a constant (terminal) velocity. At this stage
questions.A: the weight of the ball has been reduced to zero by the liquid
questions.B: the viscous drag on the ball has fallen to zero
questions.C: the weight equals the sum of the upthrust and the viscous drag
questions.D: the upthrust on the ball alone balances its weight
questions.explanation: The net force is zero at terminal velocity, so the downward weight is balanced by the upward upthrust plus viscous force.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A 50 kg girl stands on two stiletto heels each of area 1 cm². Taking g = 10 m/s², the pressure she exerts on the floor is

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The mercury column of a simple barometer becomes shorter when the barometer is carried up a high mountain because
questions.explanation: The height of the column is held up by atmospheric pressure, which falls as the mass of air above decreases.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A spring stretched beyond its elastic limit
questions.A: returns to its original length when the load is removed
questions.C: does not return to its original length when the load is removed
questions.explanation: Beyond the elastic limit the material is permanently deformed; Hooke's law applies only up to the limit of proportionality.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Glass softens gradually over a range of temperatures rather than melting sharply because it is
questions.explanation: Amorphous solids have no regular long-range structure and no fixed melting point; crystalline solids melt sharply.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A hydrometer floats deeper in kerosene than in water because
questions.A: kerosene is less dense than water
questions.B: kerosene is more viscous than water
questions.explanation: A floating hydrometer displaces its own weight of liquid; in a less dense liquid it must sink further to displace the same weight.

questions.subject: Physics

questions.subject: Physics

questions.subject: Physics

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The energy required to change 0.5 kg of water at 100 °C into steam at 100 °C is (specific latent heat of vaporisation = 2.26 × 10⁶ J/kg)
questions.explanation: Q = mL = 0.5 × 2.26 × 10⁶ = 1.13 × 10⁶ J; no temperature change is involved.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: 0.1 kg of ice at 0 °C is added to 0.4 kg of water at 30 °C in an insulated cup. The final temperature of the mixture is (L_ice = 336,000 J/kg, c_water = 4,200 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹)
questions.explanation: Heat available cooling water to 0 °C: 0.4 × 4,200 × 30 = 50,400 J; melting the ice needs 33,600 J, leaving 16,800 J to warm 0.5 kg: ΔT = 16,800/(0.5 × 4,200) = 8 °C.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: 200 cm³ of a gas at 27 °C and 1 atm is heated to 327 °C while its pressure is raised to 2 atm. Its new volume is

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A glass stopper stuck in the neck of a glass bottle can be loosened by warming the neck gently because
questions.B: the air inside the bottle escapes
questions.D: the neck expands before the stopper does
questions.explanation: Heat reaches the outer neck first and it expands, widening the hole slightly before the stopper warms up.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The linear expansivity of a metal is 1.2 × 10⁻⁵ K⁻¹. Its cubic expansivity is
questions.explanation: Cubic expansivity ≈ 3 × linear expansivity = 3 × 1.2 × 10⁻⁵ = 3.6 × 10⁻⁵ K⁻¹.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: During the day a breeze blows from the sea towards the land because
questions.A: the land warms faster, so air over it rises and cooler sea air flows in
questions.B: the sea is warmer than the land during the day and heats the air
questions.C: water evaporating from the sea expands and pushes the air inland
questions.D: the land is at a higher level than the sea, so air flows uphill
questions.explanation: Land has a lower specific heat capacity than water, so it warms faster; the resulting convection current is the sea breeze.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The silvered walls and the vacuum between the walls of a vacuum flask reduce heat transfer respectively by
questions.explanation: Shiny surfaces are poor emitters and absorbers of radiation, while the vacuum contains no material to conduct or convect heat.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A person feels cold after coming out of a swimming pool on a windy day because
questions.A: the water left on the skin is at a lower temperature than the air
questions.B: water on the skin conducts heat from the air into the body
questions.C: moving air is always at a lower temperature than still air
questions.D: water evaporating from the skin takes its latent heat from the body
questions.explanation: Evaporation is a cooling process; the wind speeds it up, so heat is removed from the skin faster.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Food cooks faster in a pressure cooker because
questions.A: the increased pressure raises the boiling point of the water above 100 °C
questions.B: the pressure forces heat into the food
questions.C: steam is hotter than boiling water at the same pressure
questions.D: the lid prevents heat loss by radiation
questions.explanation: The boiling point of a liquid rises with pressure, so the water and steam in the cooker are hotter than 100 °C.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Dew forms on grass on a clear night when the temperature of the air near the ground falls to the
questions.explanation: At the dew point the air becomes saturated with water vapour and the excess condenses on cool surfaces.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Which of the following statements explains why the temperature of the sea changes much less than that of the land between day and night?
questions.A: sea water has a higher specific heat capacity than land
questions.B: sea water is a better conductor of heat than land
questions.C: sea water reflects all the sunlight
questions.D: the sea is deeper than the land is high
questions.explanation: A large specific heat capacity means that a given amount of heat produces only a small change in temperature.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The lowest temperature recorded at a weather station was −73 °C. On the kelvin scale this is

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: On the same morning a tiled floor feels much colder to bare feet than a rug lying next to it. This is because the tiles
questions.A: conduct heat away from the feet faster than the rug
questions.B: are at a lower temperature than the rug
questions.C: absorb cold from the ground beneath
questions.D: have a lower specific heat capacity than the rug
questions.explanation: Both surfaces are at room temperature; the tiles are the better conductor and remove heat from the skin faster, which feels cold.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Fish survive in a pond whose surface has frozen because
questions.A: ice is a good conductor of heat and keeps the water below warm
questions.B: fish generate enough heat of their own to keep the water liquid
questions.C: water is densest at 4 °C, so this water sinks and only the top layer freezes
questions.D: the ice at the surface melts from below as fast as it forms
questions.explanation: Because of the anomalous expansion of water, water at 4 °C sinks and the ice forms on top, insulating the water below.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A 2 kg copper pot is heated on a stove from 20 °C to 70 °C. Taking the specific heat capacity of copper as 400 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹, the heat absorbed by the pot is

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A loudspeaker emits a note of frequency 170 Hz. Taking the speed of sound in air as 340 m/s, the distance between successive compressions in the air is
questions.explanation: Wave speed = frequency × wavelength, so λ = v/f = 340/170 = 2 m.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Sound waves are described as longitudinal because
questions.A: they can travel through a vacuum
questions.C: the particles of the medium vibrate parallel to the direction of travel of the wave
questions.D: the particles vibrate at right angles to the direction of travel
questions.explanation: In a longitudinal wave the vibrations are along the direction of propagation, producing compressions and rarefactions.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A vibrator produces 40 complete waves in 8 s on a rope, and the distance between successive troughs is 0.15 m. The speed of the waves is

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two points on a progressive wave are a quarter of a wavelength apart. The phase difference between them is
questions.explanation: One wavelength corresponds to 360°, so λ/4 corresponds to 90° (π/2 radians).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In a stationary wave the distance between two successive nodes is 0.2 m. The wavelength of the wave is
questions.explanation: Adjacent nodes are half a wavelength apart, so λ = 2 × 0.2 = 0.4 m.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A person standing round the corner of a building can hear people talking on the other side but cannot see them. This is because sound waves
questions.A: travel faster than light waves through the air
questions.B: are reflected back by the walls of the building
questions.C: are diffracted round the corner more than light waves
questions.D: are longitudinal and so can pass through the bricks
questions.explanation: Sound wavelengths (about a metre) are comparable to the size of the obstacle, so sound diffracts strongly; light wavelengths are far too small.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: When water waves pass from deep water into shallow water, their
questions.A: frequency decreases while the speed and wavelength stay the same
questions.B: wavelength increases while the speed and frequency decrease
questions.C: speed increases while the wavelength and frequency decrease
questions.D: speed and wavelength decrease while the frequency stays the same
questions.explanation: The frequency is fixed by the source; slowing down in shallow water shortens the wavelength (v = fλ), which is refraction.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The electromagnetic waves used in television remote controls are
questions.explanation: Remote controls send coded pulses of infrared radiation to the receiver.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A progressive wave is represented by y = 5 sin(200πt − 0.5πx), where x and y are in metres and t in seconds. The frequency of the wave is
questions.explanation: Comparing with y = A sin(2πft − kx): 2πf = 200π, so f = 100 Hz.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: If the amplitude of a wave is doubled while its frequency stays the same, the energy it carries becomes
questions.explanation: The energy of a wave is proportional to the square of its amplitude.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The speed of a transverse wave on a stretched string is 20 m/s. If the tension in the string is made four times as great, the new speed is
questions.explanation: v = √(T/μ), so quadrupling the tension doubles the speed: 40 m/s.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Plane water waves in a ripple tank pass through a narrow gap in a barrier and spread out in circular arcs. This phenomenon is
questions.explanation: Spreading of waves after passing through an opening (or round an edge) is diffraction, most marked when the gap is about a wavelength wide.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The Moon is about 3.84 × 10⁸ m from the Earth. The time taken for a radio signal to travel from the Earth to the Moon is (c = 3 × 10⁸ m/s)
questions.explanation: t = distance/speed = 3.84 × 10⁸/3 × 10⁸ = 1.28 s.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A mosquito's wings complete one beat every 0.004 s. The frequency of the whine it produces is
questions.explanation: Frequency = 1/period = 1/0.004 = 250 Hz.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Which of the following phenomena shows that light waves are transverse?
questions.explanation: Only transverse waves can be polarised; reflection, refraction and diffraction occur with longitudinal waves too.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A flash of lightning is seen and the thunder is heard 6 s later. Taking the speed of sound as 330 m/s, the distance of the lightning is about
questions.explanation: The light arrives almost instantly; distance = 330 × 6 = 1,980 m ≈ 1.98 km.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A man fires a gun and hears the echo from a cliff 1.5 km away. Taking the speed of sound as 330 m/s, the echo is heard after about
questions.explanation: The sound travels to the cliff and back, 3,000 m: t = 3,000/330 = 9.1 s.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The pitch of a musical note depends on the
questions.explanation: Pitch rises with frequency; amplitude determines loudness and the mixture of overtones determines quality.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A tuning fork of frequency 425 Hz produces the first resonance of an air column closed at one end when the column is 20 cm long. Ignoring end correction, the speed of sound in air is
questions.explanation: For the first resonance L = λ/4, so λ = 0.8 m and v = fλ = 425 × 0.8 = 340 m/s.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An air column closed at one end gives its first resonance with a tuning fork when it is 20 cm long. The next resonance with the same fork occurs when the column is
questions.explanation: Resonance lengths of a closed pipe are λ/4, 3λ/4, 5λ/4…, so the second resonance is at 3 × 20 = 60 cm.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The fundamental frequency of an open pipe 0.5 m long is (speed of sound = 340 m/s)
questions.explanation: For an open pipe L = λ/2, so λ = 1 m and f = v/λ = 340 Hz.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A sonometer wire 50 cm long vibrates at 256 Hz. Keeping the tension the same, the length that will vibrate at 512 Hz is
questions.explanation: Frequency is inversely proportional to length: halving the length doubles the frequency, so 25 cm.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: If the tension in a vibrating string is made four times as great, its fundamental frequency
questions.explanation: f = (1/2L)√(T/μ), so f is proportional to √T; four times the tension gives twice the frequency.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two tuning forks of frequencies 256 Hz and 260 Hz are sounded together. The number of beats heard per second is
questions.explanation: Beat frequency = difference of the two frequencies = 260 − 256 = 4 per second.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An electric bell ringing inside a bell jar becomes inaudible as the air is pumped out, although the hammer is still seen striking the gong. This shows that
questions.A: sound needs a material medium to travel through
questions.B: light needs a material medium to travel through
questions.C: the bell stops working in a vacuum
questions.D: sound travels faster in a vacuum
questions.explanation: Sound is carried by vibrating particles; with no air in the jar there is nothing to carry it, while light still passes.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The range of frequencies audible to a normal human ear is approximately
questions.explanation: Sounds below 20 Hz are infrasonic and those above 20 kHz are ultrasonic.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A person puts an ear to a railway line and hears an approaching train before hearing it through the air because
questions.A: sound travels faster in steel than in air
questions.D: the train is moving towards the person
questions.explanation: Sound travels about 15 times faster in steel than in air, so the vibration through the rail arrives first.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A stretched string has a fundamental frequency of 100 Hz. The frequency of its second overtone is
questions.explanation: For a string the overtones are integral multiples of the fundamental; the second overtone is the third harmonic, 3 × 100 = 300 Hz.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A noise-cancelling headphone produces a sound wave that is exactly out of phase with the incoming noise. The noise is reduced because of
questions.explanation: When two waves of equal amplitude meet in antiphase their displacements cancel, which is destructive interference.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A ray of light strikes a plane mirror making an angle of 30° with the surface of the mirror. The angle of reflection is
questions.explanation: Angles of incidence and reflection are measured from the normal: 90° − 30° = 60°.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two plane mirrors are inclined at 60° to each other. The number of images of an object placed between them is
questions.explanation: Number of images = 360°/θ − 1 = 360/60 − 1 = 5.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A plane mirror is rotated through 10° while the incident ray is kept fixed. The reflected ray turns through
questions.explanation: Rotating the mirror by θ changes the angle of incidence by θ, so the angle between the incident and reflected rays changes by 2θ = 20°.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A swimming pool is 2.0 m deep but appears to be only 1.5 m deep when viewed from directly above. The refractive index of the water is
questions.explanation: n = real depth/apparent depth = 2.0/1.5 = 1.33.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Light is transmitted along an optical fibre without escaping through its sides because of
questions.explanation: Light meeting the wall of the fibre at angles greater than the critical angle is totally reflected back into the core.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Light travelling inside a glass block of refractive index 2.0 is totally internally reflected at the glass-air surface whenever its angle of incidence exceeds
questions.explanation: Total internal reflection occurs beyond the critical angle C, where sin C = 1/n = 0.5, so C = 30°.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A ray of light travelling in water (refractive index 4/3) meets the water-air surface at an angle of incidence of 30°. The angle of refraction in the air is approximately
questions.explanation: n_water sin i = n_air sin r: sin r = (4/3) × 0.5 = 0.667, so r ≈ 42°.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A camera with a lens of focal length 10 cm is used to photograph a flower 30 cm away. For a sharp picture the film must be
questions.A: 15 cm behind the lens, receiving a real, diminished image
questions.B: 15 cm behind the lens, receiving a virtual, magnified image
questions.C: 30 cm behind the lens, receiving a real image of the same size
questions.D: 7.5 cm behind the lens, receiving a virtual, diminished image
questions.explanation: 1/v = 1/f − 1/u = 1/10 − 1/30 = 2/30, so v = 15 cm; the image is real, inverted and half the size (m = v/u = 0.5).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A small lamp is placed 20 cm in front of a diverging lens of focal length 10 cm. The image of the lamp is
questions.A: 6.7 cm from the lens, virtual and erect
questions.B: 20 cm from the lens, real and inverted
questions.C: 6.7 cm from the lens, real and inverted
questions.D: 40 cm from the lens, virtual and magnified
questions.explanation: 1/v = 1/f − 1/u = −1/10 − 1/20 = −3/20, so v = −6.7 cm: a virtual, erect, diminished image on the same side as the object.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An optician prescribes spectacles of power +4 D for a patient. The lenses are
questions.explanation: f = 1/P = 1/4 m = 25 cm; a positive power means a converging lens.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A converging lens is used as a magnifying glass. To see a magnified, erect image the object must be placed
questions.B: between the focal point and the lens
questions.explanation: An object inside the focal length gives a virtual, erect, magnified image on the same side as the object.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The eye focuses on objects at different distances by
questions.A: moving the retina backwards and forwards
questions.B: changing the focal length of the lens through the ciliary muscles
questions.C: changing the size of the pupil
questions.D: moving the lens towards or away from the retina
questions.explanation: This is accommodation; a camera, by contrast, focuses by moving its lens.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: When white light passes through a glass prism, the colour that is deviated most is
questions.explanation: Violet light has the shortest wavelength and the greatest refractive index in glass, so it is bent most.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A red shirt is viewed in a room lit only by pure green light. The shirt appears
questions.explanation: A red object reflects only red light and absorbs green; with no red light available, it reflects nothing and looks black.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A man 2 m tall stands 10 m from a pinhole camera whose screen is 20 cm from the pinhole. The height of his image on the screen is
questions.explanation: Magnification = image distance/object distance = 0.2/10; image height = 2 × 0.02 = 0.04 m = 4 cm.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An object is placed 10 cm in front of a concave mirror of focal length 20 cm. The image formed is
questions.explanation: An object inside the focal length of a concave mirror gives a virtual, erect, enlarged image — the principle of the shaving mirror.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A long-sighted person can read clearly only when a book is held 100 cm away. The focal length of the spectacle lens that lets him read at 25 cm is
questions.explanation: The lens must form a virtual image at 100 cm of an object at 25 cm: 1/f = 1/25 − 1/100 = 3/100, so f = 33 cm (converging).

questions.explanation: Parallel pair: (3 × 6)/(3 + 6) = 2 Ω; total 6 Ω, so the battery supplies 2 A. The p.d. across the pair is 2 × 2 = 4 V and the 3 Ω resistor carries 4/3 = 1.33 A.

questions.subject: Physics

questions.q: A current of 2 A flows through a 5 Ω resistor for 1 minute. The heat produced is

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A 100 W bulb left on for 10 hours consumes
questions.explanation: Energy = power × time = 0.1 kW × 10 h = 1 kWh (one 'unit').

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Currents of 3 A and 2 A flow into a junction and a single wire carries the current away. The current in that wire is
questions.explanation: By Kirchhoff's first law the total current entering a junction equals the total leaving: 3 + 2 = 5 A.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An electric kettle is rated 2 kW, 240 V. The current it draws is approximately
questions.explanation: I = P/V = 2,000/240 = 8.3 A, so a 13 A fuse is suitable.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A 4 Ω resistor and an 8 Ω resistor are connected in series across a 12 V supply. The potential difference across the 8 Ω resistor is
questions.explanation: The current is 12/12 = 1 A, so the p.d. across 8 Ω is 1 × 8 = 8 V (the resistors share the voltage in the ratio of their resistances).

questions.q: The energy stored in a 4 μF capacitor charged to 100 V is

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two 2 μF capacitors are connected in series. Their combined capacitance is

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A charge of 60 C passes a point in a wire in 2 minutes. The current in the wire is

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The force between two point charges is F when they are 2 cm apart. When the separation is increased to 4 cm the force becomes
questions.explanation: By Coulomb's law the force is inversely proportional to the square of the distance; doubling the distance divides the force by four.

questions.q: To convert a galvanometer into an ammeter, one connects
questions.A: a high resistance in series with it
questions.B: a low resistance (shunt) in parallel with it
questions.C: a high resistance in parallel with it
questions.D: a low resistance in series with it
questions.explanation: The shunt carries most of the current so that only a small known fraction passes through the delicate coil.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A galvanometer of resistance 50 Ω gives full-scale deflection for a current of 2 mA. The shunt needed to convert it to an ammeter reading up to 1 A is approximately
questions.explanation: The shunt carries 0.998 A while 0.002 A passes through the coil: S = (0.002 × 50)/0.998 ≈ 0.1 Ω.

questions.q: The current-voltage graph for a filament lamp is a curve that bends towards the voltage axis because
questions.B: the resistance of the filament increases as it gets hotter
questions.C: the filament resistance decreases with temperature
questions.explanation: A tungsten filament is non-ohmic: as the current heats it, its resistance rises, so the current increases less than proportionally.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The earth wire of a three-pin plug is connected to the metal casing of an appliance so that
questions.A: the appliance draws less current from the mains supply
questions.B: a fault current flows safely to earth and blows the fuse instead of shocking the user
questions.C: the appliance heats up faster when it is switched on
questions.D: the current can return to the power station through the ground
questions.explanation: The earth wire provides a low-resistance path for fault current, protecting the user from electric shock.

questions.q: A lightning conductor on a tall building has a pointed tip because
questions.A: charge concentrates at the point and leaks away, neutralising the cloud
questions.B: a sharp point attracts lightning far more strongly than a ball
questions.C: a point is much cheaper to manufacture than a metal sphere
questions.D: a sharp point melts more easily and so absorbs the strike
questions.explanation: The high charge density at a point ionises the surrounding air, quietly discharging the building and reducing the chance of a strike (action of points).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A transformer is to step down 240 V to 12 V. If its primary coil has 1,000 turns, the number of turns on the secondary coil is
questions.explanation: Ns/Np = Vs/Vp, so Ns = 1,000 × 12/240 = 50 turns.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The core of a transformer is made of thin laminated sheets rather than one solid block in order to reduce
questions.explanation: Thin insulated laminations break up the paths of the circulating eddy currents that would otherwise heat the core.

questions.q: The rule used to find the direction of the force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field is
questions.explanation: The left-hand rule applies to the motor effect; the right-hand rule gives the direction of an induced current in a generator.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A bar magnet dropped down a vertical copper tube falls much more slowly than an identical unmagnetised bar. This is because
questions.A: copper is a magnetic metal and attracts the magnet as it falls
questions.B: induced currents in the tube produce a field that opposes the magnet's motion
questions.C: the air trapped in the tube slows the falling magnet down
questions.D: the magnet loses most of its weight inside the copper tube
questions.explanation: By Lenz's law the eddy currents induced in the tube oppose the change causing them, i.e. the fall of the magnet.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The e.m.f. induced in a coil by a moving magnet can be increased by
questions.B: using a coil with more turns
questions.D: using a thicker coil wire only
questions.explanation: By Faraday's law the induced e.m.f. is proportional to the number of turns and the rate of change of flux; a faster or stronger magnet also helps.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The magnetic field lines around a long straight wire carrying a current are
questions.A: straight lines parallel to the wire
questions.B: concentric circles centred on the wire
questions.C: radial lines pointing away from the wire
questions.D: straight lines at right angles to the wire
questions.explanation: The field forms closed circles round the wire, with the direction given by the right-hand grip rule.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The angle between the direction of the Earth's magnetic field and the horizontal is called the
questions.explanation: A freely suspended magnetic needle dips below the horizontal by the angle of dip; declination is the angle between magnetic and geographic north.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Soft iron rather than steel is used for the core of an electromagnet because soft iron
questions.C: is a better conductor of electricity
questions.explanation: An electromagnet must switch on and off with the current; steel keeps its magnetism and is used for permanent magnets.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Which of the following will NOT demagnetise a bar magnet?
questions.C: placing it in a solenoid carrying alternating current and withdrawing it slowly
questions.D: storing it with keepers across its poles
questions.explanation: Keepers preserve magnetism by completing the magnetic circuit; heat, mechanical shock and a.c. fields all disorder the magnetic domains.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two long parallel wires carry currents in the same direction. The wires
questions.explanation: Each wire lies in the magnetic field of the other; for currents in the same direction the forces are attractive.

questions.q: A simple a.c. generator differs from a d.c. generator in that the a.c. generator uses
questions.explanation: Slip rings deliver the alternating output as it is; the split-ring commutator of a d.c. generator reverses the connections every half turn.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A transformer takes 200 W from the mains and delivers 160 W to a load. Its efficiency is
questions.explanation: Efficiency = output/input × 100 = 160/200 × 100 = 80%.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Electrical energy is transmitted over long distances at very high voltage in order to
questions.B: reduce the energy lost as heat in the cables
questions.D: reduce the cost of the cables' insulation
questions.explanation: For a given power, a higher voltage means a smaller current, and the I²R loss in the cables falls sharply.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The magnet of a moving-coil galvanometer has curved pole pieces with a soft-iron cylinder between them in order to
questions.B: produce a radial field so that the scale is linear
questions.C: increase the resistance of the coil
questions.explanation: In a radial field the coil is always parallel to the field lines, so the deflecting torque is proportional to the current and the scale divisions are equal.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The count rate of a radioactive source falls from 800 counts per minute to 100 counts per minute in 45 minutes. The half-life of the source is
questions.explanation: 800 → 400 → 200 → 100 is three half-lives, so one half-life = 45/3 = 15 minutes.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A radiation from a radioactive source is stopped by a sheet of paper. The radiation consists of
questions.explanation: Alpha particles are the least penetrating; beta particles need a few millimetres of aluminium and gamma rays several centimetres of lead.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In the decay ²²⁶₈₈Ra → ²²²₈₆Rn + X, the particle X is
questions.explanation: The mass number falls by 4 and the atomic number by 2, the signature of an alpha particle (⁴₂He).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: When a nucleus emits a beta particle, a neutron inside the nucleus changes into
questions.C: a proton and an alpha particle
questions.D: an electron and a photon only
questions.explanation: n → p + e⁻ (+ antineutrino); the electron is ejected as the beta particle and the atomic number rises by one.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The energy released in a nuclear reactor comes from the
questions.B: fission of heavy nuclei such as uranium-235
questions.explanation: A neutron splits a U-235 nucleus into lighter fragments, releasing energy and more neutrons that sustain a chain reaction.

questions.explanation: The missing mass has been released as the binding energy that holds the nucleus together (E = Δmc²).

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The number of neutrons in the nucleus ²³⁵₉₂U is
questions.explanation: Neutrons = mass number − atomic number = 235 − 92 = 143.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The age of an ancient wooden object is estimated by measuring the activity of the isotope
questions.explanation: Living things take in carbon-14 while alive; after death it decays with a half-life of about 5,700 years, so the remaining fraction gives the age.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The rate of decay of a radioactive sample
questions.A: increases when the sample is heated
questions.B: is unaffected by temperature, pressure or chemical combination
questions.C: decreases when the sample is compressed
questions.D: depends on the chemical compound containing the nuclide
questions.explanation: Radioactive decay is a spontaneous, random nuclear process that external physical or chemical conditions cannot alter.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A 16 g sample of a radioactive element is left for three half-lives. The mass of the element that remains is
questions.explanation: 16 → 8 → 4 → 2 g after three successive half-lives.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Which of the following detects radiation by the ionisation it produces in a gas?
questions.explanation: Each ionising particle entering the tube triggers a pulse of current that is counted.

questions.explanation: Ionising radiation kills cells; it is directed at the diseased tissue so that healthy tissue receives as little as possible.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In Rutherford's alpha-scattering experiment, the few alpha particles that were deflected through very large angles had passed
questions.A: through the diffuse cloud of electrons round the atoms
questions.B: very close to the small, massive, positive nucleus
questions.C: through the empty space between the atoms of the foil
questions.D: along the surface of the foil without entering it
questions.explanation: Only a concentrated positive charge could repel the fast, heavy alpha particles so strongly; most particles met only empty space.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Photons of energy 5.0 eV strike a metal surface whose work function is 2.0 eV. The stopping potential needed to prevent the fastest photoelectrons from reaching the collector is
questions.explanation: KE_max = hf − W = 5.0 − 2.0 = 3.0 eV, so a reverse p.d. of 3.0 V just stops the fastest electrons.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In the photoelectric effect, increasing the intensity of the incident light while keeping its frequency the same
questions.A: increases the maximum kinetic energy of the electrons
questions.B: increases the number of electrons emitted per second
questions.C: lowers the work function of the metal
questions.explanation: Each photon frees at most one electron; more photons per second mean more electrons, but each still receives the same energy hf.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: X-rays are produced in an X-ray tube when
questions.A: a heated filament glows brightly inside the evacuated tube
questions.B: fast-moving electrons are suddenly stopped by a metal target
questions.C: a radioactive source inside the tube decays and emits radiation
questions.D: ultraviolet light strikes a metal plate and releases electrons
questions.explanation: Electrons accelerated through a high voltage lose their kinetic energy on hitting the tungsten target and part of it is emitted as X-ray photons.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Pure silicon is doped with a small amount of phosphorus (a Group 5 element). The material produced is
questions.explanation: Each phosphorus atom supplies one extra electron that is free to move, so the majority carriers are negative electrons.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A p-n junction diode is forward biased when
questions.A: the p-side is connected to the positive terminal of the battery
questions.B: the n-side is connected to the positive terminal of the battery
questions.explanation: Forward bias narrows the depletion layer and lets current flow; reverse bias (p to negative) blocks it.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A single diode connected in series with a load across an a.c. supply produces
questions.D: an alternating current of doubled frequency
questions.explanation: The diode conducts during one half of each cycle only; full-wave rectification needs a bridge of four diodes or two diodes with a centre-tapped transformer.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The three terminals of a junction transistor are the
questions.explanation: A small base current controls a much larger collector current, which is why the transistor can amplify.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Unlike a metal, the electrical conductivity of a pure semiconductor increases when it is heated because
questions.A: its atoms vibrate less and so obstruct the electrons less
questions.B: more electrons gain enough energy to break free and carry charge
questions.C: its resistance is completely unaffected by temperature
questions.D: the holes in its structure disappear when it is heated
questions.explanation: Thermal energy frees electron-hole pairs; in metals heating only increases lattice vibrations and hence resistance.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The output of a two-input AND gate is 1 only when
questions.explanation: The AND operation requires every input to be high; an OR gate gives 1 when either input is high.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A large capacitor is connected across the output of a rectifier in a d.c. power supply in order to
questions.B: smooth the output by reducing the ripple
questions.explanation: The capacitor charges at the peaks and discharges slowly between them, keeping the output voltage nearly constant.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The emission of electrons from a heated metal surface is called
questions.explanation: Heating gives the free electrons enough energy to escape; this is how the cathode of a cathode-ray tube produces its electron beam.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The photoelectric effect provides evidence for the
questions.explanation: Electron emission depends on frequency, not intensity, which is explained only if light arrives in packets (photons) of energy hf.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A light-dependent resistor (LDR) is used in an automatic street-lighting circuit because its resistance
questions.A: increases as the light intensity increases
questions.B: decreases as the light intensity increases
questions.explanation: In the dark the LDR's high resistance switches the lamp on; in daylight its resistance falls and the lamp switches off.
